chapter.title: The two bazaars and their price boards

cards.body: The Sensex is just 30 companies, yet the whole country checks it like the weather. Why? In our bazaar there are two market buildings, NSE and BSE, and each hangs a price board at its gate. **The board shows the mood of the whole bazaar, not what happened to any one shop**, which is exactly why it is useful and exactly where it fools people.
cards.simpler: The Sensex is only 30 companies, yet the whole country checks it like the weather. Why? Think of the market as a bazaar with two buildings, NSE and BSE. Each hangs one price board at its gate. **The board shows the mood of the whole bazaar, not what happened to any one shop.** That is why it is useful. It is also exactly where it fools people.

cards.prompt: The gate board reads 'bazaar down 1% today'. Your cousin Meera owns 1 share of a small tea shop deep inside the lanes. What do you now know about her tea shop?

options.text: It fell about 1% too, same as the board.
Nothing for sure. The board averages the biggest shops, and hers is not on it.
It rose, because small shops move opposite to the board.

whyNot.a: That's the board's average, not Meera's shop: the board only tracks the biggest stalls, and hers isn't one of them.
whyNot.c: That's a made-up rule, not how boards work: a small shop can go either way on a day the board falls.

cards.reteach: The board at the gate is one number squeezed out of the biggest shops' prices. A tea shop that isn't on the board can rise, fall or sit still while the board moves. To know Meera's shop, look at Meera's shop.

cards.title: Two halls, two boards
cards.body:
You'd think India has one stock market. It has two buildings, both in Mumbai: the *National Stock Exchange*, NSE, and the *Bombay Stock Exchange*, BSE. Most big companies list on both, at almost the same price.

Both halls open at 9:15 am and shut at 3:30 pm, Monday to Friday, with holidays off. Outside those hours nobody can buy or sell. The board just shows yesterday's last price.

**An index is a price board**: one number built from the prices of the biggest shops. Nifty 50 is NSE's board of 50 companies. Sensex is BSE's board of 30. They move together most days because they share most of the same giants.
cards.simpler:
India has two stock markets, not one, both in Mumbai: the National Stock Exchange, NSE, and the Bombay Stock Exchange, BSE. Most big companies sell on both at nearly the same price. Both trade only 9:15 am to 3:30 pm on weekdays.

**An index is a price board**: one number made from the biggest companies' prices. Nifty 50 is NSE's board of 50. Sensex is BSE's board of 30. They mostly move together because they share the same giants.

cards.title: Priya's bank versus the board
cards.body: Tuesday, 3:31 pm. Nifty has closed 0.8% down and Priya, who bought 1 share of a bank last week, opens her app braced for red. Her bank is up 2%. It reported strong quarterly profit that morning and buyers crowded in. The board fell because two or three large IT companies had a bad day, and they weigh heavily on it. Same bazaar, same afternoon, **two different thermometers**.
cards.simpler: It is Tuesday, 3:31 pm. Nifty has closed 0.8% down. Priya bought one share of a bank last week, and she opens her app expecting bad news. Her bank is up 2%. It reported strong profits that morning and buyers rushed in. The board fell because two or three big IT companies had a bad day, and they weigh heavily on it. Same bazaar, same afternoon, **two different thermometers**.

cards.prompt: Headline: 'Sensex jumps 500 points'. Your uncle Ravi says 'every company went up today'. Which reading applies the board idea correctly?

options.text: All 30 Sensex companies rose, because the board is their sum.
The weighted average of the 30 biggest BSE shops rose. Some of the 30 may still have fallen.
Every share on BSE, thousands of them, rose by 500 points each.

whyNot.a: That's treating the board as a roll call, not an average: a few giants rising can lift it while others fall.
whyNot.c: That's confusing the board with every stall in the hall: Sensex counts only 30 companies, and points belong to the board, not to each share.

cards.reteach: A board is an average with the big shops counting more. 'Sensex up 500 points' means that average moved up. It says nothing about any single company, and nothing at all about the thousands of shares not on the board.

cards.title: Giants, points and the inspector
cards.body:
Not every shop on the board counts equally. **Bigger shops pull the board harder.** If the largest company on Nifty drops 3%, the board feels it. If the smallest of the 50 drops 3%, the board barely twitches. So 'Nifty down 0.8%' often means 'a few giants had a rough day'.

Points versus percent: if Sensex sits at 80,000, a fall of 800 points is 1%. Points are the raw number; percent tells you how big the move is. Read the percent.

*SEBI*, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, is the inspector. It writes the rules both halls follow and can fine or ban cheats. It does not stop prices falling. It stops people lying.
cards.simpler:
**Bigger companies pull the board harder.** A 3% drop in Nifty's largest company moves the board a lot. The same drop in its smallest barely moves it. 'Nifty down 0.8%' often means a few giants had a bad day.

Points and percent differ: at 80,000, a fall of 800 points is 1%. Read the percent.

SEBI, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, is the inspector. It writes the rules and punishes cheats. It stops people lying, not prices falling.

cards.body: Arjun sees 'Nifty up 1.2%' on the evening news and texts his flatmate: 'market's booming, my shares must be flying.' He opens the app. His two shares, both mid-sized companies, are down. He read the mood and assumed it was the weather at his own door. Spot it in yourself: any time you say 'the market' did something to 'my share', stop and **check that share's own price**.
cards.simpler: Arjun sees 'Nifty up 1.2%' on the evening news. He texts his flatmate: 'market's booming, my shares must be flying.' He opens the app. His two shares, both mid-sized companies, are down. He read the town's weather and assumed it was raining the same at his own door. Catch it in yourself: any time you say 'the market' did something to 'my share', stop and **check that share's own price**.

cards.prompt: A friend reads out 'Nifty closed 0.8% down'. Which of these does that line actually tell you?

options.text: The 50 biggest NSE companies, averaged with the giants counting more, ended lower than yesterday's close.
SEBI found a problem in the market and warned investors to sell.
Each of the 50 companies lost exactly 0.8%.

whyNot.b: That's the inspector's job, not the board's: SEBI polices honesty; it doesn't move or announce prices.
whyNot.c: That's the average mistaken for every member: 0.8% is the board's number, and the 50 shops each had their own day.

cards.reteach: Nifty 50 is one number cooked down from 50 prices, with the biggest companies adding the most flavour. When it closes 0.8% down, the mix ended lower. Which of the 50 fell, and by how much, you still have to look up.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
NSE and BSE are the two market halls, open 9:15 to 3:30 on weekdays, and Nifty 50 and Sensex are the boards at their gates: an average of the biggest shops, with the giants weighing most. **The board tells you the bazaar's mood, never what your one shop did.**

Tomorrow: your shares never sit with your broker. So where do they live?
cards.simpler:
NSE and BSE are the two market halls. They open 9:15 to 3:30 on weekdays. Nifty 50 and Sensex are the boards at their gates: an average of the biggest companies, with the giants counting most. **The board tells you the bazaar's mood, never what your one shop did.**

Tomorrow: your shares never sit with your broker. So where do they live?

cards.body: Tonight, search 'Nifty 50 today' and write down the percent change. Then search the share price of any one Nifty company and see whether it moved **the same way**, or not.
cards.simpler: Tonight, search 'Nifty 50 today' and write down the percent change. Then search the share price of any one Nifty company. See whether it moved **the same way** as the board, or not. One look is enough to feel the gap between the mood and one shop.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now read 'Nifty closed 0.8% down' and say what it tells you about the 50 companies behind it, and what it doesn't.
